summary: Add/adjust alerts for TP hang detection + document oncall response steps (TP-group watchdog/quarantine)
description:
Requester: SRE / Oncall Readiness

Background
- After INC-2025-02-13-us-east-tp-hang, oncall had difficulty distinguishing (a) true TP group stuck/hang vs (b) slowdowns due to overload vs (c) kernel stalls.
- Existing alerting is primarily customer-symptom-based (5xx/timeout rate), which is too late and doesn’t provide actionable next steps.

Request
1) Add/adjust alerts to detect TP hangs earlier and more precisely.
2) Document the oncall response steps (what to check, how to mitigate, when to escalate, and what NOT to do).

Scope / Requirements
A) Alert signals (proposed)
- Primary: TP-group forward-progress watchdog triggers
  - Metric: runtime.tp_group.watchdog_triggers_total (by cluster, pool, model, tp_size)
  - Alert: any sustained triggers above baseline OR > N triggers/5m per pool (see thresholds below)
- Secondary: collective latency and timeouts
  - Metric: runtime.collective.latency_ms (p95/p99) by collective type (all_reduce, all_gather) and tp_group
  - Metric: runtime.collective.timeouts_total
- Triage helpers (non-paging / dashboard panels)
  - Metric: runtime.tp_rank.tokens_emitted_total (rate) / runtime.tp_rank.step_progress (monotonic counter)
  - Metric: runtime.scheduler.queue_depth / starvation markers
  - Correlation panels: api.request_timeouts_total, api.5xx_total, streaming.disconnects_total

B) Paging policy / severity
- Paging should be based on “stuck group” likelihood rather than raw latency.
- Must avoid false positives under heavy load.

C) Oncall runbook content
- A single runbook entry linked directly from alerts with:
  - Quick classification: comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation
  - Immediate mitigations: quarantine TP groups (if available), shift traffic, reduce concurrency, temporarily disable TP for impacted pool/model route, increase collective timeout only as a last resort
  - Data to capture before mitigation: rank-level logs, last progress timestamp, NCCL async error indicators, dashboard snapshot
  - Escalation: when to page Runtime vs when SRE can handle

Suggested initial alert thresholds (to validate during canary)
- WARNING (non-paging): watchdog triggers > 2 per 10m per pool OR collective p99 > 10s for 5m
- PAGE (P1): watchdog triggers >= 5 per 5m per pool OR collective timeouts increasing for 5m AND timeout/5xx symptoms present
- PAGE (P0 candidate): watchdog triggers in >1 pool/region concurrently OR associated with widespread 5xx/timeout increase

Notes / constraints
- Dedicated environments: alert routing should be customer-aware (tagged by deployment) and avoid paging for customer-controlled tests unless impacting SLA.
- Hosted: alert routing to #incidents + SRE oncall; Runtime oncall only when runbook indicates likely runtime bug/hang.

Acceptance criteria
- New alert rules merged and deployed to prod.
- Alert message includes: definition, links to dashboard panels + runbook, and “first 3 steps” snippet.
- Runbook entry published and reviewed by SRE + Runtime (Scheduling).
- 2-week follow-up: measure false positive rate and adjust thresholds.

Owner(s)
- Primary: Sergio Costa (dashboards/alerts)
- Runbook support: Tomáš Novák (paging hygiene), Kira Thompson (runbook writing)
- Reviewers: Rafael Mendes (SRE), Sofia Ivanova (Runtime Scheduling), Omar El-Sayed (Runtime observability)

Links
- Dashboard spec: confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tp-collectives-and-scheduler-health-dashboard
- Initiative: confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/tp-group-watchdog-and-quarantine-initiative
- Debug playbook: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/debugging-tp-hangs-playbook
- Postmortem: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/2025-02-13-tp-hang-us-east-sev1
comments: 2025-02-14 (Tomáš Novák): Filing this as a follow-up from the Sev1. Current symptom alerts (timeouts/5xx) are too late; we need earlier, actionable paging on TP-group stuck conditions. Please ensure alert descriptions link to a runbook and to the TP collectives/scheduler dashboard panels.

2025-02-15 (Rafael Mendes): +1. For paging, we need a clear distinction between ‘slow’ and ‘stuck’. Let’s bias paging toward watchdog triggers / timeouts rather than raw p99 latency so we don’t page during expected overload. Also, we should route WARNING to #eng-sre and PAGE to SRE oncall; Runtime oncall only when watchdog triggers exceed threshold for >10m or when multiple pools affected.

2025-02-16 (Sergio Costa): Acknowledged. I’ll implement alert rules in observability-pack with deployment tags (hosted vs dedicated). Need metric names + labels finalized from Runtime; looping in Omar for exact series/labels (tp_group_id exposure?).

2025-02-17 (Omar El-Sayed): Metrics that will exist after runtime-1.19 patch: runtime_tp_group_watchdog_triggers_total{cluster,pool,model,tp_size} and runtime_collective_latency_ms_bucket{collective,cluster,pool,model,tp_size}. No tp_group_id label in prod for cardinality reasons; we can add exemplars/structured logs for top offenders. Suggest alert on rate of watchdog triggers + concurrent increase in api_request_timeouts_total for stronger precision.

2025-02-18 (Kira Thompson): I can draft the runbook section, but I’ll need the canonical ‘first actions’ from SRE + Runtime. Also confirm what mitigations are safe (quarantine vs restart vs traffic shift).

2025-02-19 (Sofia Ivanova): For immediate mitigations, safest is: stop scheduling onto suspected stuck groups (quarantine) if the feature is present; otherwise shift traffic away from the pool/route and reduce concurrency. Avoid increasing collective timeouts as a default response; it can mask a real hang and prolong customer impact. Escalate to Runtime if watchdog triggers persist after traffic shift or if resets spike.

2025-02-21 (Sergio Costa): Implemented new panels and draft alerts in observability-pack/pr-502. Added alert annotations linking to the TP health dashboard and placeholder runbook URL. Requesting review from Rafael + Allison for paging policy and thresholds.

2025-02-24 (Rafael Mendes): Reviewed PR. Requested changes: (1) change PAGE condition to require either collective timeouts or watchdog triggers + customer symptom correlation, (2) add auto-suppression label for known perf-canary jobs, (3) include ‘capture data before mitigation’ checklist in alert text.

2025-02-26 (Sergio Costa): Updates pushed. WARNING and PAGE alerts now have correlation logic and suppression for canary namespaces. Alert text includes the top-3 triage steps and links. Waiting on runbook URL from Kira/Tomáš to replace placeholder.

2025-03-03 (Tomáš Novák): Runbook published and reviewed: ‘TP hang response (watchdog/collectives)’ is now linked from the alerts. Includes decision tree (comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler) and mitigation steps. Please ensure alert annotations point to the final URL.

2025-03-05 (Sergio Costa): Runbook link updated in alerts. observability-pack/pr-502 merged and deployed to prod. We’ll monitor alert volume for 2 weeks and adjust thresholds if needed. Marking INT-611 resolved; follow-up to revisit thresholds after runtime-1.19 rollout is tracked in SRE weekly.

2025-03-06 (Tomáš Novák): Confirmed alert is visible in prod and routes correctly. Closing. Follow-up: watch for false positives during peak hours; if needed, add additional gating on ‘no forward progress’ logs once structured logging is fully deployed.
resolution: Implemented new TP hang detection alert rules (watchdog triggers + collective timeouts with symptom correlation), deployed updated dashboard panels, and published an oncall runbook linked from alerts. Paging policy updated to reduce false positives and include suppression for perf-canary jobs.
